newsitem.title: JAPAN: None injured in blast at Japan bureaucrat's home.
newsitem.headline: None injured in blast at Japan bureaucrat's home.

text.p: Two small homemade bombs wrecked part of a concrete wall at the home of a senior Japanese Transport Ministry official on Tuesday but no one was injured, police said.
Police said they suspected leftist guerrillas might have planted the crude timed devices at the home of Deputy Vice Minister Masanobu Koyama in Kawasaki, south of Tokyo.
The two time bombs were made from flashlight batteries and gunpowder stuffed in plastic pipes, a type often used by ultra-leftist groups, police said.

Japan's dwindling far-left groups have targeted Transport Ministry officials in a relentless guerrilla campaign since the 1960s because of the ministry's leading role in the construction of Tokyo's Narita International Airport.

The ministry has also supported moves to open Japanese civilian airports to U.S. warplanes during a future regional crisis, one of the key elements of a proposed set of new guidelines for U.S.-Japan defence cooperation revealed earlier this month.
